🧠 Crypto News Brief: Washington blinked and crypto flinched. The SEC's abrupt cancellation of its Regulation Crypto vote knocked the wind out of the tokenization trade, while a second straight day of ETF redemptions dragged bitcoin back under $63,000. Institutional builders kept building anyway. 🏛️ SEC Cancels Its First Major Crypto Rulemaking Vote The Securities and Exchange Commission abruptly scrapped the Friday open meeting at which commissioners were set to propose "Regulation Crypto" — the agency's first formal crypto rulemaking and the centerpiece of Chair Paul Atkins' agenda. The regulator cited an unforeseen scheduling issue and offered no replacement date, leaving a roughly 400-page proposal that would have created tailored offering exemptions for token issuers stranded in limbo alongside the stalled CLARITY Act. Read full story 📉 Tokenization Stocks Slide on the Regulatory Setback Bullish, Coinbase and Circle all closed lower Friday as investors marked down the near-term odds for crypto's Wall Street push. The SEC also pushed back its long-awaited "innovation exemption" covering tokenized securities trading, and analysts warned that the combination of an indefinite rulemaking delay and unresolved questions over the agency's legal authority could stretch out the adoption curve for real-world asset tokenization. More details ₿ Bitcoin Slips Under $63,000 as ETFs Post a Two-Day Drawdown Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since August 3, wiping out the whole of the previous week's rally, after spot ETFs bled roughly $192 million across back-to-back sessions — the first such stretch since late July. Cooler-than-expected U.S. producer price data lifted equities but did nothing for crypto, and derivatives desks reported growing bearish positioning even as implied volatility drifted toward 2026 lows. Read more ⚔️ Strategy Fires Back at MSCI Over Index Exclusion Threat Michael Saylor's Strategy publicly rejected MSCI's proposed "non-operating company" screen, telling the index provider it should measure markets rather than decide which assets public companies may own. The five-ratio test would delete Strategy, Metaplanet and uranium holder Yellow Cake from the ACWI IMI at the November review; JPMorgan has previously pegged the resulting forced passive selling in MSTR at around $2.8 billion. Hi Oleg,

The dog days of August haven’t slowed the private markets down one bit.

Here’s our latest Pre-IPO Briefing, and there’s plenty to cover:

- Anthropic is reportedly targeting a $2T IPO for October, according to The Financial Times. That would break SpaceX’s record as the largest public debut ever.¹
- Anysphere told staff that SpaceX is close to completing its $60B acquisition of the startup, adding that the “Cursor” brand name will likely be phased out for new products.²
- Kalshi doubled its ARR in two months thanks to World Cup wagers, surpassing $4B in July. The company is also in “advanced talks” to raise at an estimated $40B valuation.³
- OpenAI completed a secondary share sale totaling about $7B ahead of its potential IPO. Current and former employees sold stock at an estimated $852B valuation.⁴
- Panthalassa is raising $225M at an estimated valuation of nearly $2B. The new round will double Panthalassa’s valuation from just three months ago.⁵

A confidential filing doesn’t guarantee that an IPO will occur, and there’s no guarantee that Anysphere will be acquired. These reports don’t imply specific results for investors with exposure to these companies via StartEngine Private. Past performance is not indicative of future results. There's no guarantee that revenue, funding, or valuation will continue to grow for these companies, or that they’ll be profitable.

The theme this week isn't just growth; it's records falling.

Ambitions for the largest IPO in history. The biggest startup acquisition ever. Key metrics doubling inside a single quarter.

The private markets are where this cycle's ceilings keep being raised, long before any opening bell. Forbes highlights Wall Street's biggest names advancing tokenization this week, Ondo among them.

final-email (https://d5vnWT04.na1.hubspotlinks.com/Ctc/RM+113/d5vnWT04/VVmpxj92NfZlW7GMgtk1gCpljW2lg-cV5SLQkNKqQ43lcq-W69sMD-6lZ3lkW1DF2y_35pnqLW4BRknZ62gV9dW3btmGZ9b9RT-N3cz7yNcRl63W5ZYbnf6V2klWW7Kglks3B6TkFW1nmsgC3m4gwXN3C0Q3Zppz1-W3cGCB_32PmT6N33WQJrL1Fv-W5mz8-H2hVvLlW4gNP-Q5nlGNHW39Tqx81zR9t1N55mDMXsZ-SkW6077w02X7dbrW3CQcth1DKhntW7qcjZB2sVcdhW60R6tF5hNFRdW2JTdRj3lzcgBW7s22Mn11GRVVdSkql-04 )

A Wall Street Business, Not a Crypto Slogan

Tokenization has arrived on Wall Street, and this week’s news from Nasdaq to Franklin Templeton proves the point.

“The next generation for markets.”

According to BlackRock's Larry Fink, tokenization is “the next generation for markets.” A recent Forbes article (https://d5vnWT04.na1.hubspotlinks.com/Ctc/RM+113/d5vnWT04/VVmpxj92NfZlW7GMgtk1gCpljW2lg-cV5SLQkNKqPP5jMY8W5BWr2F6lZ3kVW2qTKpB4vdCw6W3M8rJw1lh459W8mNLkt378B0_W8vbHZm5XpkHYW8-QzhF4-zPxyW100ttf1HVs3_W1Dgvb11bfWqlW8g98Yw1Sx7pwN83-2083ZDB2W8gCPvG3F9prjN38HBjS_sXJyW6gDcgt8qxmTBW93dKDH7D-1kFW2-j8sb5W89LBN2JvmDyw6KqlW4XdJbF6-dJS_W6zDgc74f2D-WW4ZB0s147L2gCW2z1yms4XwkbRN6sZnXg2ZQRHW4R3mPl1xVC5RW60-v3t6FpXR6W14fkBr1Y5zs1N8JsmNHc1PZvW8P_n6h6b3sS6W82RLSb4hxNkXW95p2t_14Y7gWW3l88bK4DS-LVW67T4Cw4b76nNW3Djwld6ZLLckW6ZpmB6887klzVjJ7cD2Sn1vzW3dx8d47c1mW3W1rV3jG1X8NY9f2TXFXP04 ) highlights the accelerating adoption of tokenization, with JPMorgan moving $7B daily onchain, Citi projecting $5.5T tokenized by 2030, DTCC launching tokenized settlement, and Wells Fargo tokenizing deposits this fall. Forbes also cites Ondo’s USDY as among the largest tokenized Treasury funds.

Industry News

1

Nasdaq Advances 24/7 Tokenization Push

Nasdaq announced it has agreed to acquire (https://d5vnWT04.na1.hubspotlinks.com/Ctc/RM+113/d5vnWT04/VVmpxj92NfZlW7GMgtk1gCpljW2lg-cV5SLQkNKqRz3lcq-W95jsWP6lZ3pnN4G2sCpcXvkpW2Lf5KP9jM4gRW3N3mWq5HN9fGVpf2mq7mSBhZW3R_3L37svWzhVL59k59fbd0SW6VPFPb4F3rYvW61pHw19kSw7xW5cBwmr8VGQLGN4hMb-BH_MSKW757n1_1g86gmW87MtlH71BJPfW92BjHB1yPK42W1ltbLF5nzqD6W68-v3s30s6R6W85DG4G3hdxdTW1p_jlG5S_VsmW3hwSc550Y15JW5dY3028nyptFW7d5g5m3drsYlW46_2Mn5V84frW8SphBv8GSffgW6hdsZD2Hz0hWW8XTKrN2gDbQLW40VYf67HXpbxW2zJJfZ3R2Yn7W5Y3kTy6_LQf1W7mmKlM1Y2CXWVRCNlq8m3wwdW67bXDw6DrDsmf7W1bF-04 ) the third-largest alternative trading system in the US, the LeveL Markets ATS, which has 2,500 institutional clients. Nasdaq aims to bridge the divide between digital and traditional trading with “programmable, always-on market infrastructure.”

2
